chunks: And through his chain, from Al-Asam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'I travel to Arjān, and my heart pulls me toward the grave of your father. However, when I go out, my heart is trembling and apprehensive until I return, fearing the ruler, the governors, and the armed men, until I return.' He said, 'O son of Bukayr! Do you not desire that Allāh sees you fearing for us? Do you not know that whoever fears out of fear for us, Allāh will shelter him under the shade of His Throne, and Al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) will be conversing with him beneath the Throne? And Allāh will secure him from the terrors of the Day of Resurrection; people will be terrified, but he will not be terrified. And if he is terrified, the angels will strengthen him and calm his heart with glad tidings.'

key_terms.الارجان: Arjān, a region in Iraq known for its marshes and historical significance
key_terms.قَبْر أَبِيكَ: The grave of your father (Imam Ali or specifically Imam Husayn in this context of Ziyarah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husain with fear of rulers?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam Al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) addresses the psychological burden of visiting the grave of Imām Ḥusayn (a.s.) during periods of political oppression, transforming fear of the Sultan into a spiritual virtue. He promises that such fear, when rooted in love for the Ahl al-Bayt, results in divine shelter under the Throne, intimate conversation with Imām Ḥusayn, and immunity from the general terror of the Day of Judgment, highlighting the Shia concept of *khawf* (fear) as a means of spiritual elevation.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far narrated to me from his father, from ‘Ali ibn Muḥammad ibn Sālim, from Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād Al-Basri, from ‘Abdillāh ibn ‘Abdil Raḥmān Al-Asam, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I said to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “I (often) travel to Arjān and my heart pulls me toward going to the Ziyārah of the grave of your father (Ḥusain (a.s.)). However, when I go, I am afraid; I dread the rulers, their governors, and their armed men until I return.” Imam (a.s.) said: O son of Bukayr! Do you not want Allāh to see you in fear for us?! Do you not know that Allāh will shelter those who are in fear because of our fear under the shade of His Throne, and that Ḥusain (a.s.) will be speaking to them under the Throne?! (Do you not know) that Allāh will keep them safe from the terrors of the Day of Judgment?! They will not be afraid while others will be terrified. And if they do get scared, the angels will pacify them and soothe their hearts by giving them glad tidings.
